title: Explicit partial contraction for ordered join chains
statement:
Let $r\geq1$ and let $X_0,\ldots,X_{r-1}$ be sets with specified elements $v_i\in X_i$. Let $J_{-1}=\mathbf Z[\varnothing]\cong\mathbf Z$, let $J_q$ for $0\leq q<r$ be the abelian group of finite formal integer sums of symbols $[(i_0,x_0),\ldots,(i_q,x_q)]$ with $0\leq i_0<\cdots<i_q<r$ and $x_j\in X_{i_j}$, and put $J_q=0$ otherwise. The indicated symbol families are specified $\mathbf Z$-bases in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Define $d$ by alternating deletion of vertices, including $d[(i,x)]=[\varnothing]$ and $d[\varnothing]=0$. Define the degree-one homomorphism $c_i$ to be zero on symbols containing color $i$; on a symbol missing color $i$, insert $(i,v_i)$ in its increasing-color position $k$ with coefficient $(-1)^k$. In particular $c_i[\varnothing]=[(i,v_i)]$. Define $R_i$ on symbols missing color $i$ to be zero, and on a symbol containing color $i$ to be that symbol minus the symbol obtained by replacing its color-$i$ vertex by $(i,v_i)$. Put
$$S=\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}(R_0\circ\cdots\circ R_{i-1})\circ c_i,$$
where the empty composite is the identity and the rightmost map is applied first. Then $d^2=0$ and
$$dS_q+S_{q-1}d=\mathrm{id}_{J_q}\qquad(-1\leq q\leq r-2),$$
with $S_{-2}=0$. For every family of maps $u_i:X_i\to Y_i$, with chosen elements $w_i=u_i(v_i)$ in $Y_i$, the induced homomorphisms $J_q(u)$, defined by applying $u_i$ to vertices, satisfy $J_{q+1}(u)S_q^v=S_q^wJ_q(u)$. The displayed formula for $S$ expands on each basis symbol into a finite integer sum of basis symbols obtained only by inserting chosen vertices or replacing vertices by chosen vertices; the coefficient list and the choices of insertions and replacements depend only on $r$ and the list of colors, not on any equality tests among the $x_j$ and $v_i$.

proof.text: All maps are defined first on the specified bases, then extended by finite integer linear combination. This gives well-defined homomorphisms: for $d$ there are $q+1$ terms, for $c_i$ at most one, and for $R_i$ at most two. By [def-weil-pbc-free-module], uniqueness of the finite basis expansion shows that two such homomorphisms agree once they agree on every basis symbol. Hence the following calculations on symbols prove identities on the groups; all maps on zero groups are zero.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ordered-join-single-color-identities] to the specified sets and vertices. Its differential and insertion/remainder formulas are exactly those of the item, so it gives $d^2=0$ and $dc_i+c_id=1-R_i$ in every integer degree, including the augmented and top degrees.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent ordered-join expansion; repair assembly step 2, covering original calculations 2-4.

proof.text: Prove the ordered-prefix algebra directly for the existing integer-linear maps. From the single-color identities and d squared zero, expand both dR_i and R_i d as d-dc_id. Induct on prefix length using P_(n+1)=P_nR_n to get dP_n=P_nd. Distribute the sum defining S and substitute dc_i+c_id=1-R_i. Its terms are P_i-P_(i+1), whose finite sum is 1-P_r. On a face missing j, induct on n>j: the final factor either kills the face or produces a difference with the same color set, so P_n kills it by induction. In degree q≤r-2 each symbol has fewer than r colors, so choose a missing color and apply this argument; linearity gives P_r=0. Degree -2 has no symbols, so its contraction is zero. This direct calculation avoids constructing a ChainComplex and transporting its integer-indexed components.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent ordered-join expansion; repair assembly step 3, covering original calculations 5-6.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-ordered-join-functorial-expansion], $J(u)$ commutes with each $c_i$ and $R_i$. Substituting these identities successively into the ordered composite gives $J(u)P_i^v c_i^v=P_i^w c_i^wJ(u)$; adding over $i$ gives the required naturality of $S$. The same lemma gives every individual summand as either zero or the signed subset list $(-1)^{k_i+|A|}\sigma_{i,A}$. Concatenate these finitely many lists over $i$; their sum is $S\sigma$, and their coefficients and replacement/insertion choices depend only on $r,C$, even when output symbols coincide. For the empty symbol only $i=0$ contributes, so $S_{-1}[\varnothing]=[(0,v_0)]$, consistently with the augmented identity.
